new_entities.name: Dapagliflozin in non-diabetic chronic kidney disease
new_entities.description: Use of dapagliflozin in adults with chronic kidney disease who do not have type 2 diabetes.

new_entities.name: Kidney outcomes
new_entities.description: Clinically important kidney outcomes such as sustained eGFR decline, end-stage kidney disease, or kidney-related death.

edges.effect_quant: DAPA-CKD showed a lower primary kidney composite with dapagliflozin overall (HR 0.61), and the prespecified non-diabetic subgroup had an even stronger relative effect (HR 0.50). In the biopsy-confirmed FSGS subgroup, kidney-outcome estimates still favored dapagliflozin (HR 0.62), though with wide confidence intervals because of small sample size.
edges.population: adults with albuminuric chronic kidney disease without type 2 diabetes, including mixed non-diabetic CKD etiologies and smaller glomerular-disease subgroups
edges.mechanism: SGLT2 inhibition reduces intraglomerular pressure and tubuloglomerular stress and may slow kidney-function loss even in the absence of glucose-lowering needs.
edges.summary: This is one of the major practice-changing kidney-protection signals of the last few years. The effect clearly extends beyond diabetes, which is why the non-diabetic subgroup result matters so much here.
edges.caveats: The evidence is strongest for albuminuric CKD already on standard care, and some rarer etiologies rely on smaller subgroup analyses. The edge should not be generalized too casually to every low-albuminuria or ultra-advanced CKD scenario.

evidence.citation: Heerspink HJL et al 2020 N Engl J Med
evidence.notes: Dapagliflozin in Patients with Chronic Kidney Disease. DAPA-CKD.

effect_quant.comparator: primary kidney composite outcome in DAPA-CKD with dapagliflozin versus placebo
